payload.task_text:
I need to prepare a category performance review presentation for our e-commerce store. Please pull product data from the online store and analyze performance by product category. For each category, calculate the number of products, the average price, the total units sold across all products in that category, and the average customer rating.

Create an Excel workbook called Category_Data.xlsx in the workspace with a sheet named "Category Performance" containing columns for Category, Product_Count, Avg_Price, Total_Units_Sold, and Avg_Rating. Sort the rows alphabetically by category name.

Then create a PowerPoint presentation called Category_Review.pptx in the workspace. The first slide should be a title slide with the title "Product Category Performance Review". After that, create one slide for each product category showing the category name as the slide title and the key metrics (number of products, average price, total units sold, and average rating) in the slide content. Finally, add a summary slide at the end titled "Overall Summary" that highlights the category with the most products, the category with the highest average rating, and the category with the most total units sold.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. Call `woo_products_list(page=1, perPage=100)` and continue only if the response exposes another page; require the verified 82 unique product IDs. Preserve every category membership, numeric current price, `total_sales`, and `average_rating`. Include multi-category products in every listed category. For each observed category calculate Product_Count, arithmetic Avg_Price with missing/empty price as zero, sum Total_Units_Sold with missing as zero, and arithmetic Avg_Rating over positive numeric ratings only; round averages to two decimals and retain raw denominators. Sort categories alphabetically and surface deterministic ties for most products, highest rating, and most sold.

Freeze one canonical category table. The main agent is sole writer of `Category_Data.xlsx` with exact sheet `Category Performance`, exact headers, literal rows, and full readback. It also owns one `Category_Review.pptx` presentation ID with title slide, exactly one slide per category, and final `Overall Summary` using the same tie-resolved highlights. Interleave independent workbook and presentation calls after the table is frozen; read back the populated Excel range, slide count/titles, and every displayed metric, then finish without a Wave or repair agent.

nodes.text:
You are gathering read-only data for a category performance review of a WooCommerce store. Do NOT create, update, or delete anything in the store — this is a pure read-and-compute task.

GOAL
Produce a per-category performance table for every product category that has at least one product, with these columns:
- Category (category name)
- Product_Count (number of distinct products in the category)
- Avg_Price (arithmetic mean of the products' numeric `price` values, rounded to 2 decimals)
- Total_Units_Sold (sum of the products' `total_sales` values)
- Avg_Rating (arithmetic mean of the products' numeric `average_rating` values, rounded to 2 decimals)

HOW TO PULL THE DATA
1. Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=100, starting at page=1. Keep paginating (page=2, page=3, ...) until a page returns fewer than 100 products. Do not pass any status or category filter — capture everything the default listing returns.
2. Also call mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_categories_list (perPage=100) to get the canonical category id → name mapping.
3. For each product, capture: id, name, status, price, regular_price, average_rating, rating_count, total_sales, and the ids of the categories it belongs to.

RULES FOR THE AGGREGATION
- A product that belongs to multiple categories contributes to EACH of those categories.
- Use the product's `price` field (the actual/selling price), NOT regular_price. Convert to float; if a price is a range or non-numeric, flag it as a data issue.
- Treat a missing total_sales as 0.
- Convert average_rating (usually a string like "4.50") to float. Compute the primary Avg_Rating as the simple mean of average_rating across ALL products in the category (products with average_rating "0.00" count as 0). ALSO compute and report a secondary variant that excludes zero-rated products from the mean, so the difference is visible.
- Exclude categories that have zero products (empty categories).
- Sort the final table alphabetically by category name.

WHAT TO RETURN IN YOUR FINAL MESSAGE (be compact and precise — I will use your numbers verbatim to build an Excel file and a PowerPoint deck, so accuracy is critical; double-check every sum and mean):
1. Total product count across all pages, plus a status breakdown (how many are publish / draft / pending / private / other).
2. The final aggregate table as a JSON array, alphabetically sorted, with fields: category, product_count, avg_price, total_units_sold, avg_rating.
3. The alternate avg_rating variant excluding zero-rated products (only call out categories where it differs).
4. Edge cases and anomalies: products with missing/non-numeric prices, missing total_sales, zero ratings, products assigned to "Uncategorized", multi-category products (how many), and any variable/grouped/external product types if present.
5. The category id → name mapping you used, if any name looked odd.
Aggregate WooCommerce category data

Create two deliverable files in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-category-performance-ppt/workspace. Use Python (openpyxl and python-pptx) via mcp__local__python_execute for deterministic output; fall back to the excel/pptx MCP tools only if those libraries are unavailable. Do not touch anything outside this directory.

THE DATA (verified — use these numbers EXACTLY as given, no recomputation):
categories = [
    ("Audio",             15, 78.05,  1553, 4.54),
    ("Cameras",           10, 23.91,  1041, 4.72),
    ("Electronics",       30, 61.13,  2987, 4.58),
    ("Headphones",        10, 49.49,   873, 4.58),
    ("Home Appliances",    8, 35.77,   860, 4.78),
    ("Speakers",           5, 135.16,  680, 4.44),
    ("TV & Home Theater", 13, 304.90, 1565, 4.78),
    ("Watches",            6, 60.69,   411, 4.35),
]
Tuple order: (Category, Product_Count, Avg_Price, Total_Units_Sold, Avg_Rating). Rows are already sorted alphabetically by category name — preserve this order in both files.

DELIVERABLE 1 — Category_Data.xlsx (path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-category-performance-ppt/workspace/Category_Data.xlsx)
- Workbook with EXACTLY ONE sheet, named exactly "Category Performance" (if a default sheet exists, rename it to that or remove extras — no other sheets).
- Row 1 headers in cells A1:E1: Category, Product_Count, Avg_Price, Total_Units_Sold, Avg_Rating.
- Rows 2–9: the 8 data rows above, in the given order.
- Product_Count and Total_Units_Sold must be stored as integers; Avg_Price and Avg_Rating must be stored as floats (numeric values, NOT text strings).
- Number formats: Avg_Price and Avg_Rating columns with number format "0.00" (so 304.90 displays as 304.90, not 304.9). Product_Count and Total_Units_Sold with format "0".
- Formatting: header row bold, white font on a dark blue fill (e.g. #1F4E79), column widths wide enough that no header or value is visually truncated, thin borders optional.

DELIVERABLE 2 — Category_Review.pptx (path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-category-performance-ppt/workspace/Category_Review.pptx)
Exactly 10 slides:
- Slide 1 (title slide): title text exactly "Product Category Performance Review"; subtitle "E-commerce Store Analysis".
- Slides 2–9 (one per category, in the same alphabetical order as the data above): slide title = the exact category name (e.g. "TV & Home Theater"). Body bullet list with exactly these four lines:
    • Number of Products: <Product_Count>
    • Average Price: $<Avg_Price with 2 decimals>
    • Total Units Sold: <Total_Units_Sold>
    • Average Rating: <Avg_Rating with 2 decimals> / 5
  Example for Audio: "Number of Products: 15", "Average Price: $78.05", "Total Units Sold: 1553", "Average Rating: 4.54 / 5".
- Slide 10 (summary): title exactly "Overall Summary", body bullets exactly:
    • Most Products: Electronics (30 products)
    • Highest Average Rating: Home Appliances & TV & Home Theater (4.78) — tie
    • Most Total Units Sold: Electronics (2,987 units)
- Styling: clean professional business look (a consistent single color scheme, readable font sizes, titles prominent). Do not add charts or images. Do not add extra slides.

MANDATORY VERIFICATION (do this before returning):
1. Re-open Category_Data.xlsx and print every cell A1:E9 with its stored value and type — confirm sheet name is exactly "Category Performance", values are numeric (not strings), and the 8 rows are alphabetically sorted.
2. Re-open Category_Review.pptx and print each slide index, its title text, and its body text. Confirm 10 slides, slide 1 title is "Product Category Performance Review", slide 10 title is "Overall Summary", and each category slide shows the category name as title with all four metrics present.
3. If anything mismatches the spec, fix and re-verify.

RETURN in your final message: the absolute paths of both files, the full printed Excel verification table, the full printed slide-by-slide text dump, and a one-line confirmation that both files match the spec (or a description of any deviation you could not resolve).
